title: smart-routing-fallback-incident-breadcrumbs-zoe
content:
Quick summary:
- Notes + breadcrumbs from debugging the 2026-02-12 regional failover where smart-routing fallback caused increased 503/timeout rate for a subset of hosted-api requests.
- Drafty, rough — keeping the commands tried, raw errors, and hypotheses together for handoff.

Timeline (local TZ, PST):
- 2026-02-12 09:11: first spike in 5xx from US-west region; alerts from console route-level SLO.
- 2026-02-12 09:13: automated fallback policy kicked in (policy=prefer-latency->fallback=reduce-quality-model).
- 2026-02-12 09:14: burst of 503s reported by proxy pool; affected customers reported degraded chat responses.
- 2026-02-12 09:22: SRE team disabled smart-routing fallback manually to stop oscillation.

What I saw in the metrics:
- Per-route latency histogram shifted right around 09:11 and latency p95 jumped from 220ms to ~1.1s.
- Backend server error rate (5xx) for model-onnx-v2 increased from 0.2% -> 5.6% in 2 minutes.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped from 87% -> 32% on affected nodes.

Commands and logs I ran (raw):
- curl to the gateway to reproduce a single failing request:
  curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -d '{"model":"model-onnx-v2","input":"hello"}'
  -> HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
  Response body: {"error":"backend_unavailable","detail":"no healthy backends for model-onnx-v2/us-west-2"}

- Checked gateway routing decision for a single request (debug endpoint):
  curl -s "https://gateway.internal/debug/routing?model=model-onnx-v2&region=us-west-2"
  -> JSON-ish debug (truncated): routing_decision: fallback_to_model=model-quant-v1 reason=insufficient_capacity target_pool=pool-dedicated-3

- kube logs from the serving pod (short):
  kubectl -n serving logs pod/serving-onnx-5f7c8dbc --since=1h | grep -i error | tail -n 40
  2026-02-12T09:10:43Z ERROR kvcache: failed to read prefix cache: redis connection timeout (host=redis-cache-1:6379)
  2026-02-12T09:10:44Z WARN router: backend pool pool-hosted-usw-2 unhealthy: too_many_conns
  2026-02-12T09:11:01Z ERROR model-server: failed open_stream: downstream closed; upstream=pool-hosted-usw-2 slot=123

- redis ping from node (to sanity check connectivity):
  redis-cli -h redis-cache-1 ping
  -> PONG
  (but connection timeouts seen intermittently in pod logs)

- netstat / conntrack quick check on node: showed many CLOSE_WAIT sockets to backend inference nodes (approx 2.2k) at peak.

Other artifacts I inspected quickly:
- LB health checks: several failed health checks for pool-hosted-usw-2 around 09:09-09:13.
- Autoscaler logs: reported scale-up events but nodes were not joining cluster (timeout to reg service).
- Recent deploy: model-onnx-v2 changed kernel selection flags 02-10 (PR #2142).

Error snippets (copied directly):
- gateway: {"ts":"2026-02-12T09:12:05Z","level":"error","msg":"no healthy backends","model":"model-onnx-v2","region":"us-west-2"}
- serving runtime stack (abridged):
  E022 09:10:58.123 node_manager.cc:412] Failed to register node: timeout contacting registry (err=ETIMEDOUT)
  E022 09:11:03.987 batch_scheduler.cc:279] Failed to acquire slot: pool-hosted-usw-2 overloaded

Hypotheses (rough order):
1) KV cache instability increased cold-starts -> more heavy inference requests -> backend saturation. Evidence: kvcache timeouts in pod logs and reduced cache hit-rate.
2) New kernel selection (PR #2142) increased per-request memory footprint or connection patterns causing more CLOSE_WAITs and backend overload. Evidence: recent deploy and odd socket patterns.
3) Autoscaler/registration race: nodes failing to join due to registry timeouts, so capacity reported but not actually available. Evidence: node_manager register timeouts in logs and autoscaler entries.
4) Health-check flapping combined with routing fallback policy created an oscillation: when gateway sees some backends unhealthy it triggers fallback to quantized model, which has different resource profile and caused further pressure on the remaining backends (circular effect).

What I tried / quick experiments:
- Replayed failing request against other region (us-east-1) with same model -> success, latency stable.
- Increased gateway timeout and retry threshold (local test) -> reduced 503s for ~10s but didn't fix root cause.
- Temporarily disabled fallback policy (on test cluster) -> routing remained on primary model, load concentrated and still caused backend queueing.
- Rolled back PR #2142 on a single canary node pool to check mem/cpu pattern -> canary showed lower CLOSE_WAIT and lower mem usage (limited test data).

Notes / things to check next (TODO):
- Re-run jstack / strace on a jammed backend process to confirm socket states and whether they are waiting on epoll/blocked syscalls.
- Capture full tcpdump for 2-3 minutes at 09:09 window on a sample host to see handshake/connection resets.
- Check kernel version and ulimit settings on hosts; confirm no recent infra change (kernel tuning) coincident with deploy.
- Verify redis client library version used by kvcache; see if there was a transient regression.
- Reproduce locally with load-generator and reverted kernel flags to compare memory and fd usage.
- Verify autoscaler logs more thoroughly (why nodes didn't join): registry auth? DNS? reg-service latency?

Notes to SRE / oncall handoff (if needed):
- If this recurs in prod: temporarily blacklist pool-hosted-usw-2 from routing and scale up dedicated pools in us-west until root cause addressed.
- Prefer not to keep fallback policy disabled for long — it helps continuity for other classes of failure. If disabling, document for product impact.

Rough conclusions for postmortem draft:
- Root cause likely interplay of kvcache instability + new kernel selection PR increasing resource usage + intermittent node registration timeouts. The fallback policy amplified the impact by shifting load to pools with different characteristics and creating a feedback loop.

Open questions (for the triage):
- Did any infra maintenance run in us-west around 09:00 (kernel upgrades, iptables changes)?
- Are we certain the PR #2142 changes cannot be toggled at runtime (feature flag)? If not, consider hotfix to force previous kernel selection on affected pool.
- Is health-check frequency/threshold tuned properly for our quick autoscale? Too aggressive flapping can cause false positives.

References / links: see linked_artifacts above. Also see Slack thread INF-4823-discuss for live notes.

Personal notes: keep this doc messy — will fold into proper postmortem (shared_drives/incident-postmortems) after syncing with Marcus + Ethan.

-- ZP
